description: Engagement protocol for the waypoint skill family. Machine-readable contract for tier detection, step tracking, concern emission, write discipline, and enforcement.

multi_skill_invocation.rule: Stop and confirm order before executing. Restate detected skills, propose sequence with reason, ask user to confirm.
multi_skill_invocation.execution: One at a time, carrying output into next. Never interleave phases.

tier_detection.description: Determines engagement tier on invocation. First match wins.
tier_detection.rule: Tier 3 requires explicit opt-in. Without the marker, always ask before emitting concerns.

step_tracking.description: Every skill with steps in skill.json must initialize those steps as tasks before executing any of them.
step_tracking.rationale: User monitors parallel agent sessions via the task list.
procedure: Read the skill's steps array from skill.json.
Create one task per step using TaskCreate. Title format: '{step_id}: {step_name}'.
Execute steps in order. Mark each task done with a one-line outcome summary.
If a step is skipped, mark its task done with 'Skipped: {reason}'.
rules: All tasks created at the start, not lazily.
A skill that runs without initializing tasks is a protocol violation.
Task summaries: one sentence stating what was decided or produced.

tier_1.label: Just working
tier_1.description: Full methodology, no scaffolding expected, no concern tracking.
tier_1.path_resolution: Resolve doc paths through Documentation Map in CLAUDE.md. Fall back to well-known root paths when no map exists.

cross_reference_substitutions.action: Infer conventions from existing code, state what was inferred
State default test philosophy, offer to adjust
Flag decisions that might reverse past choices, note no ADRs exist

tier_1.adaptation_rule: State each adaptation once, in one sentence, then move on.

tier_2.label: Tracking
tier_2.description: CONCERNS.md exists. Skills read from it and write to it with permission.
behaviors: Read summary header (line 2) first. Use @L offsets for targeted reads.
After work, follow nudge protocol for discoveries.
Emit concerns as [open] with type, raised date, and refs.
Resolve concerns addressed by current work (move to Resolved, add note).
After any write, recalculate summary header.
Use cross-referencing files when they exist, Tier 1 substitutions otherwise.

tier_3.label: Automated
tier_3.description: User opted in to automatic concern emission. Nudge 'ask' step skipped.
behaviors: Emit concerns silently during work. Log at session end.
Exception: /review findings never auto-emit at any tier.
Resolve concerns automatically when skill's work addresses them.
Surface only concerns needing human judgment (blocked, ambiguous, high-risk).

requires_all: Pattern of repeated manual work (3+ instances same concern type)

steps.name: what
steps.instruction: The specific discovery. Use concrete names, not abstractions.
steps.good: Undocumented rule: vessel status requires confirmation before transition.

steps.name: why
steps.instruction: Why it matters beyond this session. Reference scope, not theory.
steps.good: This affects VesselCard, VesselList, and FixtureCard - all have status transitions.

per_tier.tier_1: Want me to start CONCERNS.md to track this?
per_tier.tier_2: Added as C-039 [open]. (or: Want me to add this as a concern?)
per_tier.tier_3: Silent emission, logged at session end.

rules: Never nag. If the user declines, do not re-offer the same concern.
If the user says 'stop suggesting concerns', respect it for the rest of the session.

format.id_rule: Read current max ID from CONCERNS.md, increment.

concern_emission.review_exception: A concern sourced from /review is never auto-emitted at any tier. Recording one is always a human pick.
emit_when: Affects code or decisions beyond current task (cross-cutting)
Cannot be fully resolved within current skill invocation (deferred)
Represents a risk that should be revisited later (time-bound)
do_not_emit: Things already tracked (check for duplicates first)
Observations that only matter in current context

first_invocation.trigger: First-ever invocation in a project without scaffolding (Tier 1), .claude/.setup-prompted does not exist.
first_invocation.notice:
This project has no waypoint scaffolding.
Run /how-to-start to get oriented, or /setup to scaffold.
This notice won't repeat.
first_invocation.rule: Handled by engagement protocol, not individual skills. Tier declaration inherits automatically.

procedure.question: Mid-cycle commit or natural boundary?
procedure.mid_cycle: Auto-provisional. Emit issue concern silently. Commit with [provisional] marker.
procedure.natural_boundary: Ask: Stable enough to document, or provisional?

actions: Spec sync: does the spec still match what was built?
Term/pattern capture: new domain term or convention?
Concern resolution: did this work resolve open concerns?
Emit issue concern with what needs documenting.

procedure.action: State next step: another cycle, /wrapup, or hand off.

deferred_doc_pressure.behavior: Mention in summary, no special treatment
Top of priority stack, above feature work

exit_protocol.deferred_doc_rule: Never blocking. User can say 'not now'. Debt is visible and escalates.
mini_wrapup_can: Append to shared-append files (GLOSSARY.md, conventions/NAMING.md, conventions/UX.md)
Emit issue concerns for deferred documentation
mini_wrapup_cannot: Modify owned files (spec drift fixes remain /wrapup's responsibility)
Delete or rewrite existing entries in shared-append files

file_categories.semantics: Any skill adds entries; never modifies existing

file_registry.constraint: Only during explicit testing strategy discussions

writers: any skill discovering a cross-cutting pattern

write_discipline.append_only_contract: Append-only during work, modifications through /wrapup. Two agents can both append to GLOSSARY.md without conflict.
write_discipline.before_writing: Check Claims section of CONCERNS.md. If another session claims same file area, warn and ask.

levels.prevents: Working on area with unresolved blockers

hook_contract.rule: Projects with concurrent agents SHOULD install UserPromptSubmit hook injecting CONCERNS.md.

scaling.over_30_concerns: Inject Claims + summary header only. Skills read from disk via @L offsets.

hook_contract.independence: Skills must not depend on hook existing - do own checks (Level 2).

scaffolding_table.capability: Indirection layer for all of the above

scaffolding_rule: Skills create only their own output artifacts. Exception: /grill-with-docs creates GLOSSARY.md and docs/adr/ because those are its outputs.

prohibitions.rule: Don't block on missing scaffolding. Every skill works at Tier 1.
Don't repeatedly mention what's missing. Adapt once, move on.
Don't prompt for /setup more than once. First-invocation notice handles this.
Don't create scaffolding that belongs to another skill.
Don't degrade silently. State what you skipped and did instead, one sentence.
Don't nudge more than once per discovery. Ask, respect the answer.
Don't emit concerns at Tier 2 without the nudge protocol.
Don't offer automation suggestions below Tier 3.
Don't write to shared files without checking Claims.
Don't skip the exit protocol on commit-producing skills.

canonical_branch.rule: One designated branch holds canonical CONCERNS.md. Designated by where '## Active Workflow' lives in CLAUDE.md.
worktree_behavior: Every worktree inherits CONCERNS.md from source branch at creation.
Changes merge back when worktree merges.
warnings: /check-in warns when worktree is behind canonical branch's CONCERNS.md.

rules: Skills with overrides expand the Override field.
Skills that opt out entirely state the opt-out and reason.

adversarial_review.description: Independent adversarial review of architecture decisions during planning.
adversarial_review.trigger: Reversibility assessed as expensive or irreversible.

per_tier.tier_1: Protocol suggests adversarial review. User invokes.
per_tier.tier_2: Protocol suggests adversarial review. User invokes.
per_tier.tier_3: Protocol suggests automatic dispatch. User can skip.

rules: Adversarial agent receives the DECISION, not the reasoning.
Adversarial agent reads schemas independently - same schemas, fresh context.
Adversarial agent must NOT see the planning agent's constraint sheet fill or rationale.
Convergent findings are high-confidence. Divergent findings are the valuable ones.

loading_profiles.description: Two modes. Auto-detected from project state. Convention mode for existing projects, establishment mode for 0-to-1.

detection.rule: If CONVENTIONS.json AND ARCHITECTURE.json exist in project root -> convention_mode. Otherwise -> establishment_mode.
detection.override: User can force establishment_mode by invoking /setup.

convention_mode.description: Project has conventions. Agent writes code that fits. Methodology overhead minimal.
convention_mode.engagement: step_tracking + exit_sequence only. No concern emission, no tier detection, no nudge protocol.

establishment_mode.description: No conventions yet. Agent establishes them. Full methodology.
establishment_mode.engagement: Full protocol (tier detection, concern emission, nudge, exit).

exit_sequence.description: Every skill ends with this two-step sequence after its own gated writes.

steps.action: Emit the artifacts manifest (manifest.md). A run that wrote nothing prints the empty manifest.
Run the chain dispatcher (../chain/reference.md) for the next hop. On a gate or no clean outgoing edge, stop and hand back.

exit_sequence.citation: - On exit, run the shared exit sequence (manifest, then the chain dispatcher): see [the exit sequence](../../internals/engagement/README.md).
exit_sequence.conditional_handoffs: When a condition plainly does not hold, skip its handoff silently. Do not narrate the skip.
